newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow says terms agreed for NATO-Russia council.
newsitem.headline: Moscow says terms agreed for NATO-Russia council.

text.p: Russia and Germany finalised plans on Tuesday for the first meeting of a Russia-NATO partnership council giving Moscow a say in the Western defence alliance's affairs.
The council, created under an agreement signed by President Boris Yeltsin and NATO leaders in May, will meet at ambassadorial level in Brussels on Thursday.

The Russian and German foreign ministers, Yevgeny Primakov and Klaus Kinkel, also confirmed after talks at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport that the council's first meeting of foreign ministers would take place in New York in September.
"We agreed how the first Russia-NATO meeting under the permanent joint council will go ahead," Primakov told an airport news briefing.
He said he had also discussed details of the first ambassadorial meeting with visiting U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright at the weekend and British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook on Monday.
The joint Russia-NATO council is intended to improve cooperation between the former Cold War foes and gives Moscow a say, but not a veto, in alliance security matters.
Primakov and foreign ministers from the 16 NATO member states will meet during a session of the United Nations General Assembly which starts on September 16.
"We will consider the situation in Bosnia and the peacekeeping operation in broader terms," Primakov said.
He said efforts to tackle international terrorism and organised crime would also be on the agenda.

Primakov clashed with Albright and Cook over swoops by NATO peacekeepers last week on two suspected Bosnian Serb war criminals. He said Moscow had not been consulted over the raids and that they threatened the peace process in Bosnia.
A NATO representative visiting Moscow said Bosnia might also be raised at Thursday's session of the council in Brussels.
"It would seem to be a subject that could come up," John Barrett, head of NATO's policy planning and speech-writing section, told a news conference. He gave no more details.
